note: A width-generic Verilog module toward VHDL, and the design that found hif-backend#93. hif2vhdl encoded the parameter as a 32-bit signed generic with a bit-string literal default and rewrote every port bound as to_integer(W - "0000...0001"); vhdl2hif accepted it and hif2verilog then aborted in sortParameters with "Unable to get type of value". It now writes `W: integer := 5` and the bound `W - 1`. Hand-written VHDL spelling the same thing as `generic (W : integer := 5)` round-tripped through those two tools cleanly, so the defect was hif2vhdl's encoding and not hif2verilog's handling. W is 5 rather than a power of two so a silently substituted width is a different number, and `top` reads a[W-1] so the parameter must reach the body and not only the port list. Distinct from parameterized/parameterized_width.v, a bare .v on plain_roundtrip that never simulates.
